directives.text: We'll run add x3, x1, x2: add the values in registers x1 and x2 and put the sum in x3. Right now x1 = {x1} and x2 = {x2}.
Fetch: the PC holds address {pc.addr}. Instruction memory returns the 32-bit word stored there, {imem.instr}.
Decode: the word's fields say this is a register–register add that reads x{decode.rs1} and x{decode.rs2} and writes x{decode.rd}.
Read: the register file puts {regfile.rdata1} and {regfile.rdata2} on its two output buses.
Memory: add doesn't load or store, so data memory sits idle this cycle.
Write back: the result goes into x3, which now holds {x3}.
Advance: the PC moves to {pc}, the next instruction. Every instruction runs through these same phases.

presentation.prompt: Why does the CPU need registers?

directives.text: The ALU can only work on values wired right next to it. Registers are a handful of fast slots inside the CPU; memory is far larger but slower to reach, so instructions bring values into registers, compute there, and store results back only when they need to.

presentation.prompt: What actually happens inside the adder?

directives.text: Each full adder adds one bit of a, one bit of b and a carry in, producing a sum bit and a carry out for the next bit. Thirty-two in a chain make the 32-bit adder. Subtraction reuses it: a − b is a + (not b) + 1.

presentation.prompt: What happens if the number gets too large?

directives.text: x3 has 32 bits, and read as a signed number its top bit is the sign. 2,147,483,647 is the largest positive value: every bit below the sign is 1. Adding 1 carries into the sign bit, so the same 32 bits now read {x3}, the most negative value. No bit is lost; the sum is too large for the signed range. RISC-V doesn't stop on this; programs that care check for overflow themselves.

assumptions: Single-cycle and unpipelined: one instruction finishes before the next starts.
A subset of RV32I: add, sub, and, or, xor, slt, addi, lw and sw.
Eight words of data memory; misaligned or out-of-range accesses fault instead of trapping.
Physical detail (transistors, wire delay, power) needs a separately grounded model and is not shown.
